title: Data Management & Sharing - Frequently Asked Questions
bodyHtml:
We are interested in multiple types and levels of collaboration. If you are interested in submitting data, see below for instructions. If you are interested in contributing a bioinformatic method or a visualization, or in working with us to develop the Knowledge Portals, please email us at help@kp4cd.org.

Data Sharing and Upload

The knowledge portal represents results from genetic and genomic data. Although you are welcome to submit individual level data, only summary level data will be made available.

What kinds of data can I share?

  • Genetic data:
    • variant-level associations summary statistics
    • gene-level associations summary statistics
    • credible sets
  • Functional genomic data:
    • gene expression
    • accessible chromatin
    • variant-gene linkages
    • chromatin states
    • binding sites
    • results of computational methods

If you want to provide download links instead of integrating your data in our portal, we can accept additional data types (for example, polygenic risk score results).

How do I upload my dataset?

The data coordinating centers are at the Broad Institute and UCSD (CMDGA).

There are multiple ways to transfer your data:

  1. Copy them over to our Broad directory if you have access to the Broad server
  2. Provide a download link (for example, on your own platform, or dropbox, or google drive)
  3. Use ASPERA site transfer (more secure and can handle more data than google drive)
  4. Reach out to someone on the team at help@kp4cd.org.

Are there limits on the size of the data?

There are currently no limits on the size of the data, but we recommend you always zip your data for easy transfer. 

How do I write my data management and sharing plan using your resource?

See template available here.

Does it cost me to share data with you?

No, there is no fee for sharing your data.

How do I access/preview data after uploading?

You can view the results of your data on the portal. This is a collaborative process. We will work with you to represent your data successfully. Once your data has been received, we will send you a protected preview link to access it before it is shared publicly on the portal. 

Data Management and Access

How will you protect my data?

  • Only summary level analysis will be displayed on the portal. We will never show individual level data.
  • We have analyzed the privacy risks inherent in sharing summary statistics in the Knowledge Portals and found them to be extremely low. Read our white paper here.
  • Learn more about our policies on data transfer, use, and protection here.

What can’t you do for me? What is not in scope?

  • We don't ingest all data types. See above for data types that we accept.
  • We cannot write a DMS plan for you, but we are happy to work with you to complete one. See above for templates.

How do I ensure my data will be made accessible and accessibility will be maintained?

Our project is an NIH-approved data repository. As such, we are committed to maintaining FAIR principles, including open access to data. The Knowledge Portal resource has had stable funding, and we plan to continue through renewals and by obtaining additional funding. We do not anticipate that the resources will be decommissioned.

How do I reference these data?

Different data types may be viewed on various portal pages. Your contact on the KP team will let you know where the data can be viewed.

Regulatory Compliance and Data Restriction

What compliance/regulatory documents are needed to submit individual-level data to the Common Metabolic Diseases Knowledge Portal?

  • In order to include individual-level data in the CMDKP, you will need to obtain permission from your institution's IRB (or your country's equivalent) to share the data with us and make summary level metrics available on the Portal.
  • For more information on the data policies of the CMDGA, click here.
  • In order to ensure proper protection of your data, we have a Data Transfer Agreement that must be executed.

What will you do with my data?

  • For individual-level data, we will perform quality control and association analysis in order to generate summary-level data for display on the Portal.
  • All data types submitted to the Portal are included in multiple bioinformatic analyses.
  • You will have the opportunity to review the results before any data are made available on the Portal.

What if my data can’t come to the United States?

A Federated Node at EMBL-EBI allows data to be stored there and be accessed by the Portal. In the future, we plan to release technology that will support additional federated nodes in other locations.

Are you a NIH repository?

Yes, the Common Metabolic Diseases Knowledge Portal (CMDKP) is a NIH-supported scientific data repository. See a sample NIH Data Management and Sharing Plan here.

Can I control access to my results?

Yes, you control access to your results.

Do you submit to other repositories for me?

No, you are responsible for submitting to other repositories. Please let us know if you have any questions or concerns.
